target_customer: Clinics, gyms, longevity and wellness practices and health professionals who prescribe nutrition and exercise
problem: Metabolic testing (VO2max, resting metabolic rate) was gold standard but confined to sophisticated labs; PNOE made a portable clinical grade breath analyzer for practices.
business_model: Hardware device sale plus software subscription and expert support
product_category: Breath analysis and metabolic testing device

founders.name: Apostolos Atsalakis
founders.background_notes: A search snippet says the idea grew from PhD work at Cambridge; source not opened

founders.name: Panos Papadiamantis
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the name

technical_complexity.rationale: Required a medical grade gas analysis sensor, hardware design and validation against lab reference systems, plus software.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware validation and clinic software create some barriers, but established metabolic cart makers existed and no FDA clearance was found by a directory.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; incumbents kept selling stationary and mobile carts.

market_need_then: YC page says metabolic testing was valuable but underutilized and limited to sophisticated clinics.

branding.name_origin: Search results describe pnoe as an ancient Greek word meaning breath; no company statement found

identity.logo: Wordmark PNOĒ with a macron over the E
identity.visual_style: Dark on light, clinical but modern

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive Greek-rooted word with a macron that signals breath; the macron adds typing friction and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: PNOE is active with about 70 staff and says more than 3,000 health professionals use it. Funding figures conflict across aggregators and trade press, so the funding story is unverified. The company appears to have grown by selling a portable validated device to clinics and gyms ahead of the longevity trend, though no primary funding source was opened.
notes: Unverified: a $5.8M seed in 2019 appears only on aggregators (Seedtable, VCBacked); CB Insights says $10.45M over 5 rounds; Endeavor about $10.7M; a TechCrunch 2026 search snippet says about $22M including an $11M round. No round recorded. Competitor list empty: only CB Insights and company-authored comparison pages (undated, current) name COSMED, Cortex, Korr, Lumen. Founder backgrounds not found on opened pages. Downgraded to depth 1 by orchestrator: the researcher reported combining the outcome and branding searches.
